lines: Friend, Paul stands up in that synagogue and squeezes Israel's WHOLE history into it: Egypt, the wilderness, the judges, the kings. And all of it leads to one name: Jesus, the Savior God promised from David's line (Acts 13:17-23).

Here's the difference Paul hangs everything on. David served God's purpose, fell asleep and saw decay. Jesus? God raised Him from the dead, and He did not see decay (Acts 13:36-37). God kept His promise to the fathers by raising Him up (Acts 13:32-33).

So what does that mean for you and me? Through Jesus, forgiveness of sins is proclaimed, and everyone who believes is justified from everything the law of Moses could never justify them from (Acts 13:38-39). Not "everyone who stamps perfectly." EVERYONE WHO BELIEVES. As a stamper who spent years behind the takeout menus, friend, that's my favorite part of the whole sermon.

Then watch what happens. Same message, two reactions. Some people urge Paul and Barnabas to bring it back next Sabbath, and some are filled with jealousy and contradict it (Acts 13:42-45). Same batch of cookies: one person asks for seconds, the next one sends the plate back to the kitchen.

But rejection doesn't stop the word. It sends it OUTWARD, because the Lord had already said, “I have made you a light for the Gentiles, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.” (Acts 13:46-47). The Gentiles rejoice, and the word of the Lord spreads throughout that region (Acts 13:48-49).

Paul and Barnabas get driven out of the district, and the disciples are still filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit (Acts 13:50-52). Somebody runs ME out of town, I'm pouting in the back of a drawer for a month. These disciples? JOY.
And Paul and Barnabas are already headed to Iconium (Acts 13:51). The road isn't done with them yet, friend.
